en: Now, therefore, we shall set forth the supplementary rules (*pārṣada*) for the study of the *Nyāya*. 1. One should know the *saṃhitā* (euphonic combination) of words. 2. [The rule] regarding the formation of words (*padavidhi*). 3. Words beginning with *bṛhaspati* have two acute (*udātta*) accents. 4. For words ending in *-pratyañc*, the penultimate syllable has two accents. 5. When there is a single substitute (*ekādeśa*), there is a specific rule regarding the vowel *ā* occurring between vowels of the *a*-series. 6. And likewise when it follows a word ending in a vowel of the *a*-series. 7. And when it begins with the vowel *i*. 8. And when it begins with the vowel *e*. 9. When a word ending in a *kṛt* suffix is preceded by two prepositions (*upasarga*). 10. When a verbal root (*dhātu*) is preceded by a gati particle. 11. When a verb (*ākhyāta*) is preceded by a preposition. 12. In each instance of utterance, the preceding [syllable] [is accented]. 13. Two [syllables] are accented by one [rule]. 14. Those consisting of two *natika* measures.

15. Or [the first word is unaccented] when it is a causal agent (parakāraṇa). 16. Or when it is a secondary instrument (parayogin). 17. In verses consisting of four quarters (*arthapāda*), a verb (*ākhyāta*) or a vocative (*āmantrita*) at the beginning of a quarter is acutely accented. 18. Words such as *vyāghra* (tiger) at the beginning of a quarter are unaccented, except where an exception has been stated. 19. In cases of syntactic inversion or elision of words, the accentuation is as if they were at the beginning of a quarter. 20. Due to connection with *ca*, there is no loss of accent (*anighāta*). 21. Due to connection with *vā*, there is no loss of accent. 22. After a vocative that is acutely accented on its first syllable, [the following is unaccented]. 23. Those whose case-endings (*karaṇa*) are elided, or those that lack endings, [are treated as such]. 24. Due to connection with another [word], there is no loss of accent. 25. [Words] joined with *na hi* [are unaccented]. 26. [A word] joined with *yat* when it is compounded [is unaccented]. 27. By express statement, [a word] by what follows [is unaccented].
And [the rule] is applicable everywhere, whether it be a general rule, an exception, or an elided word by which the connection occurs. Thus ends the first quarter.

29. The plural form is used for the word *dviṣ* (enemy). 30. A vocative case ending is always acute-accented, whether it is singular (*daivam*) or dual (*daivī*). 31. [The first syllable of a word] is acute-accented when it denotes an unequal division of a whole (*ardha*). 32. A neuter noun, or a generic term (*jāti*) meaning "belonging to this" (*tasyedam*), has its final syllable acute-accented. 33. [The following words] have their second syllable acute-accented. 34. After the prohibition regarding the vowel *a*, the subsequent syllable of words beginning with *ajara* is acute-accented. 35. A word ending in *a* is [acute-accented on the penultimate] in the sense of "Brahmā" or "of Brahman. 36. The neuter word *brahma* has its initial syllable acute-accented. 37. [The following words] have their final syllables acute-accented. 38. The word *kāvyā* has its final syllable acute-accented when it is a proper name and not a literary work. 39. The word *dakṣiṇā* has its final syllable acute-accented when it ends in a secondary derivative suffix (*taddhita*). 40. The word *āśā* has its final syllable acute-accented when it expresses a blessing (*āśis*).

*arvācīnam* is either a different suffix (*pratyaya*) [or a compound] 41; *maho devasya mahato devasya* 42; there is elision of the letter *t* and the final acute accent (*antodāttatva*) 43. Thus ends the second quarter.

The original accent of the first member of a compound is set aside by this [the following rules]. 44. Verbs that resemble nouns are unaccented. 45. The particle *kam* is unaccented. 46. The particle *yathā* is unaccented. 47. Verbs resembling gerunds (*upasarga*) are unaccented. 48. Vocatives distinguished by their accent are unaccented. 49. This is an exception to the rule concerning the beginning of a verse-quarter (*pāda*). 50. Those [vocatives] which have a circumflex (*svarita*) on the first syllable are unaccented. 51. Monosyllabic words with a circumflex are unaccented. 52. Words with a circumflex [on the first syllable] are unaccented. 53. In the second person plural, those [verbs] containing two *y*s are unaccented. 54. In all genders and numbers, when not in a compound, [the word] *tanvā upaspṛśata* is unaccented. 55. There are four [cases], and the *kṣaipra* [circumflex] occurs; in the five types of *padya*, those beginning with the final acute (*antodātta*) apply, as does the [rule] for the letter *u* everywhere. 57.
The first chapter of the *Prātiśākhya-mūla-sūtra* belonging to the *Atharvaveda* is completed.

1. *Kanyalā*. 2. In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the substitution of case-endings begins with the letter *e*. 3. Elsewhere, [the root] *sacati* [is used]. 4. In the form *ākam*, there is the elision of the letter *m*. 5. According to Śākalya, in cases such as *iṣv-ādiṣu*, there is the substitution of the subsequent form (*pararūpa*). 6. The letters *ī* and *ū* also occur in the sense of the locative case (*saptamī-artha*). 7. In the sense of "before" (*pūrva*), [the word] *sayakāra* [is used]. 8. Is there the elision of the letter *y*, or is it a different suffix (*pratyaya*)? 9. Or is it an exception (*apavāda*)? 10. The term *vṛṣabha* is a designation of a deity. 11. From the root *as* (to be), the second person singular imperative (*madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana*) is used in the sense of commanding (*praiṣaṇya*). 12. The words *iti* and *itaḥ* are used elsewhere [than in the aforementioned senses]. 13. Other [words] follow after or precede. 14. There are others ending in the diphthong *ai*.

In the section on *kārābādha* (14): those [stems] which have *ā* as their penultimate vowel and end in *m* are feminine singular; those with a short penultimate vowel are masculine. This is the first quarter.

16. Those ending in a sibilant (*ūṣman*) have their vowel-endings obstructed. 17. In case of doubt regarding elision (*lopa*). 18. In case of doubt regarding the third [case], those ending in *s* as well. 19. And those ending in *ā* which cause the elision of suffixes (*pratyaya*). 20–1. A verb (*ākhyāta*) ends only in the letter *g*. 20–2. In the past tense (*bhūta*), the singular of the second person (*madhyama*) [is used]. 21. *Enā* is unaccented (*anudātta*). 22. Those ending in *ut* [are so] when followed by *s*, and when at the beginning of a conjunct consonant (*saṃyoga*). 23. And when followed by a word beginning with *ś*. 24. *Viśva* ends in a visarga (*visarjanīya*). 25. Those ending in a vowel (*svarānta*) have their vowel-endings obstructed by those ending in *ūṣman* or *ṣṭu*. 26. *Enā* has its final syllable accented (*antodātta*). [Those] ending in a vowel, when followed by *s*.

27. And at the beginning of a conjunction [of words], as in "gopā me stam abhūtam" (protect me, you two have become [protectors]), there is the dual ending. 28. The singular, dual, and plural endings ending in sibilants (*ūṣman*) [occur]. 29. Except for those following "prapā," "kṛpā," "deva," and "gopa," others ending in *p* with a sibilant [occur]. 30. "Bhūridhārā," "śatadhārā," and "madhudhārā" are singular forms. 31. Feminine plural forms ending in sibilants [occur]. 32. "Stanayan" (thundering) and so on; "vṛṣṭyā," "parjanyasya vṛṣṭyā," and "abhīpato vṛṣṭyā" are in the instrumental case. 33. "Grāhyāmitrānyāhyā," "gṛhā," and "grāhyenaṃ vidhyāmi" [occur]. 34. [End of section.]

"By means of this earth, with the essence of the earth, I unite thee with the earth; [I unite] the earth with the earth, with the sky, with the earth"—thus [he says]. (35) "These are your names, O rivers; you are all these; he who knows them all, may he go to them; all those are placed in Yama"—these are neuter plural forms. (36) Thus ends the second quarter.

37. A long vowel [is substituted] before a *bhūta* [word]. 38. [The substitution occurs] after words beginning with *aṅga* when they denote a limb (*aṅga*). 39. In the Vedic language (*chandas*), [the same applies]. 40. [The substitution occurs] for that which ends in *a*. 41. *Eṣaḥ*, *saḥ*, and *vyañjane* [are pragṛhya]. 42. But in the case of a single substitute (*ekādeśa*), [the preceding vowel is pragṛhya]. 43. [The same applies] after the vowel *ā*. 44. Also after a word ending in a *kṛt* suffix and after a word ending in any other consonant. 45. *Enā*, *ehā*, and so forth, remain in their original form (*prakṛti*). 46. These [words] among the *pragṛhya* are followed by *patih* [as a second member], provided it follows words such as *bhūta*; the second member is udātta on its first syllable. 47. Words containing two *y*s. 48. [Words] containing two *j*s. 49. [Words] containing two *l*s. 50. [Words] containing two *p*s. 51. [Words] containing two *t*s. 52. [Words] containing two *n*s. 53. [Words] ending in *e*. 54. [Words] consisting of multiple parts (*nānāpada*). 55. [The rules apply] to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).

The second-person singular imperative endings ending in *a* (praiṣaṇya) [are unaccented]. (56) A word from the Naighaṇṭuka list (naigamī) [is unaccented] when there is no *t* following it. (57) Words ending in a circumflex (*svarita*) accent, when followed by an acute (*udātta*) in sandhi (*saṃhitā*), [become unaccented] when they form a single phonological unit (*ekādeśa*) with that acute. (58) When a prohibition is expressed, the substitute for the first-person pronoun (*asmad-ādeśa*) [is acute]. (59) [Words] containing a pause (*avagraha*) before the syllable *ṅa* [are unaccented]. (60) And when there is a pause before the syllable *na*, the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*) is maintained. (61) [Words] containing a pause before the syllable *ma* [are unaccented]. (62) [A word is unaccented] when preceded by the prefix *su*. (63) [A word is unaccented] when preceded by the word *sva*. (64) Thus ends the third quarter (*pāda*).

65. [The substitution of *dadāti* occurs] before a *sārvadhātuka* suffix. 66. [The substitution of *rayim* occurs] before *dā* when it denotes the past. 67. When there is a word-intervening between two words that are in apposition (*samānādhikaraṇa*) and have the same meaning, the forms beginning with *śata* are treated as such even with this intervention, and they are oxytone (*antodātta*). 68. When the remainder is elided (*luptaśeṣa*), there is an elision (*ava-graha*) and the original form (*prakṛti*) is substituted. 69. The following words are masculine: *danta*, *pāda*, *hṛdaya*, *udaka*, *nāsikā*, *sahasra*, *māna*, *rātri*, *jāyā*, *dāru*, *māsa*, *puṃs*, *śeku*, *kṛcchra*, *māvat*, and *gambhīra*. 70. And when there is the elision of *n*, the form *pāda* is used. 71. Also in *dīrghāyutvāya* and similar forms. 72. In the case of the root *pātayati*, the vowel of the medicinal herb (*oṣadhi*) is lengthened. 73. The root *pādayati* occurs in other contexts. 74. [End of section].

Except for *padyati*, [there are] seventy-five [words] containing the letter *s* (76). In the sense of "in that" (*tam*), [the following applies]: when a word ending in *añc* follows a nominative (*prathamānta*) form, it is divided in two ways; [this occurs] in the case of the nominative plural (*uttama*) among nominatives (78). [This applies] to words ending in *t* (79), and to those ending in *n* when there is no obstruction by *m* (80). [There are] those ending in *m* (81) and those ending in *n* (82). Thus ends the fourth quarter. The second chapter of the *Ātharvaṇa-Prātiśākhya-Mūlasūtra* is completed.

1. In the case of vowels that possess a voiced sound and have *r* as their original form; 2. And indeclinables; 3. The vowel *o* in a vocative remains in its original form (*prakṛti*) when followed by *it*, except in Vedic (*ārṣa*) usage; 4. The root *dadhāti* preceded by *api*; 5. The root *ā-dhā* when it is part of a compound ending in *ita*; 6. Words similar to those that undergo reduplication (*āmreḍita*), provided they are not themselves reduplicated; 7. Due to the occurrence of *ṣatva*, *ṇatva*, protracted vowels (*upācāra-dīrghatva*), and the attainment of euphonic combination (*samāpatti*); 8. In the word *kṛṇotu*; 9. A short vowel occurs in the sense of the suffix *mat*; 10. Regarding the *visarjanīya* in *saṃhitā*; 11. The final syllable is acute (*udātta*); 12. A short vowel occurs in the second member of a compound (*uttarapada*); 13. There is *vṛddhi* of the initial syllable; 14. Elongation (*dīrgha*) occurs frequently before a word beginning with *y*; 15. In *gaviṣṭau*.

In *gaveṣaṇa*, there is no elision of the letter *v*. (15) In *śapatheyyaṃ sahaśeyyāya*, the letter *y* follows the vowel *e*. (16) Both the preceding and following vowels are short. (17) The letters *a* and *i* are augmentations of the preceding [vowel]. (18) In *vidhema*, it is otherwise. (19) [The rule applies] after those ending in the vowel *a*. (20) And also after those ending in the vowel *e*. (21) And also after those ending in the vowel *o*. (22) Thus ends the first quarter.

23. The root *hṛṣ* preceded by the prefix *ut-* [forms *ut-harṣita*]. 24. Singular forms [are used] except in other cases. 25. [The suffix] ending in *t* [is applied]. 26. The suffix *su* is optionally not elided after a word ending in a *ṅ* (nasal) or after a *kṛt*-derived form. 27. Words beginning with *e* [are used] in the past tense (*hyastanī*). 28. Analysis (*vigraha*) occurs with a verb and a preposition (*upasarga*). 29. And [analysis occurs] with an indeclinable (*avyaya*). 30. According to the grammatical treatise (*yathā-śāstra*), there is a desire for conjunction (*saṃyoga*). 31. A *t* sound occurs between two *r* sounds. 32. An *s* sound occurs between two *r* sounds. 33. In the sense of "renown" (*khyāti*), the forms *khyau* and *khyayau* occur; [the form] *śuśruṣī* occurs as an exception (*bādhau*) from the root *śuc*. 34. A consonant cluster (*saṃyoga*) ends in *y*. 35. A consonant cluster ends in *h*. 36. [The suffixes] *tam* and *am*. 37. [The suffixes] *mam* and *au*.

37. *kanau* (the two *na*s); 38. *panau* (the two *na*s); 39. a conjunction beginning with *ka*; 40. a conjunction beginning with *ra*; 41. the letter *tī* in *kṛttīrdūrśānī*; 42. the letter *ya* in *yo aśvyena*; 44. [the letters] in *vikāre’vayave*; 45. the two *ṇya*s in *haraṇyair*; 46. the two *ma*s in *tāmradhūmrā*; 47. the absence of the letter *ya* in *nadyo veśantyā iva*; 48. the instrumental case-ending in *tvaṣṭreva rūpam*; 49. the two *dha*s in *aparudhma*; 50. the two *la*s in *kalmaliḥ kuñjalam*; 51. the two *ta*s in *satte*; 52. the letter *ra* in *ārdrahastā samaṅta*.

A conjunction beginning with the letter *ṅ* [is a case of hiatus] 52; *tiryaṅ* [becomes] *tirau* 53; *ṛbhvāṇaṃ mātaribhvarī* [becomes] *mātaribhavī* 54; and *antavañcā samante pra yaddhandiṣṭho jihvāṃ ni tṛndhi* [becomes] *pra yan na dandiṣṭho jihvāṃ ni tṛndhi*, where it begins with the letter *n* 55. Thus ends the second quarter.

56. The *visarjanīya* replaces the letter *n*. 57. The letter *r* replaces the letter *n*. 58. When preceded by a short vowel, [the *visarjanīya*] remains in its original form (*prakṛti*) before a dental stop (*tavarga*). 59. Before a word beginning with a long vowel, the *visarjanīya* of the seven verbal roots [remains as *s*]. 60. In a compound, the *sakāra* [replaces the *visarjanīya*] according to the joints of the parts (*yathāparu*), except before *k* and *p*. 61. [The *sakāra* replaces the *visarjanīya*] when followed by a word in the fifth case (*pañcamī*). 62. This is an exception to the rule for the substitution of *ṣ*. 63. The *ṣakāra* [replaces the *visarjanīya*] when it is not a prefix (*anupasarga*). 64. [The *ṣakāra* replaces the *visarjanīya*] after a preceding member of a compound (*pūrvapada*). 65. There is a lengthening of the vowel in a prefix (*upasarga*) when followed by a subsequent member of a compound (*uttarapada*). 66. There is a lengthening of the vowel in the subsequent member when it is not a word denoting movement (*aniṅgya*), and also in words denoting movement (*iṅgya*). 67. There is a lengthening of the vowel in a reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).

In the Vedic language (chandasi): [the initial vowel of] words beginning with *aśva* [is optionally long] before the suffix *matup* (68); [the initial vowel of] all genders and numbers [is optionally long] before the suffix *matup* (69); [the initial vowel of] the first [member of a compound] [is optionally long] (70); [the initial vowel of] the second [member of a compound] [is optionally long] (71); [the initial vowel of] the first syllable of the second member of compounds beginning with *sātrāsāha* [is optionally long] (72); [the initial vowel of] the word *nāman* becomes short at the end of a compound (73); [the initial vowel of] the first syllable of the second member of compounds consisting of particles (*nipāta*) or indeclinables (*avyaya*) [is optionally long] (74). Thus ends the third quarter (pāda).

76. In the case of *añcat*, when the suffix has been elided, the vowel is not lengthened. 77. In a *devatā-dvandva* (compound of deity names), [the first member] is long before the endings *abhiḥ*, *bhyām*, *bhyas*, and *su*. 78. A monosyllabic word that undergoes *vṛddhi* [is long]. 79. A monosyllabic word ending in a vowel other than *a* [is long]. 80. [The rules apply] with respect to specific vowels, genders, accents, case-endings, and numbers. 81. In Vedic usage (*chandas*), there is the transposition of phonemes, genders, accents, case-endings, and sentences. 82. Omissions and additions of phonemes, short, long, and protracted vowels, and the distinction between *ātmanepada* and *parasmaipada* endings also occur. Thus ends the fourth quarter.
Thus the third chapter is completed; the root sūtras of the Prātiśākhya in the Atharvaṇa Saṃhitā-lakṣaṇa treatise are finished.
